                     <ns0:hi>Capernaum</ns0:hi> was a City <ns0:hi>lifted up to Heaven,</ns0:hi> for mer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cies of all sorts, which Christ foretold, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.23. should be brought down to Hell for their contempt of his Doctrine and Miracles.                <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ And the Jews passover was at hand: and Jesus went up to Hierusalem <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Concerning the Jewish <ns0:hi>Passover,</ns0:hi> we have once and again spoken in our Notes on the other Evangelists; the Institution of it, was <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.                <ns0:p n="16">16 And said unto them that sold doves. Take these things hence: make not my Fathers house an house of merchandise <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">At this his first coming, he gives them that sold <ns0:hi>Doves</ns0:hi> a liberty to take their goods away; but at the last coming, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.12. it is said, <ns0:hi>he overturned their seats.</ns0:hi> Those that think this president sufficient to vindicate <ns0:hi>private Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons</ns0:hi> tumultuous pulling down Images, seem not to consi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der, that Christ was no private Person (tho so esteemed) and did what he did as Lord of his house: Those who urge it, as inferring <ns0:hi>Magistrates</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Superiors</ns0:hi> duty in this case; urge it well; for it may well be from hence concluded, That it is the Will of Christ, that places set a part for <ns0:hi>publick Worship,</ns0:hi> should neither wickedly be made Dens <ns0:hi>of Thieves,</ns0:hi> nor yet <ns0:hi>indecently</ns0:hi> made places for men to buy and sell in; tho we can ascribe no such holiness to any place, as to the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> which had not only a particlar Dedication, but was built by Gods order, his acceptation of it declared, and had peculiar Promises annexed to it; besides its Prefigura<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of Christ (of which we shall speak more afterwad); yet even nature it self teacheth, That there is a decent re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verence and respect due to such places. This Action of Christs, also, before he had published the Doctrine of the Gospel, instructs us, That those who have authority, are not always to refrain from removing instruments of Superstiti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on and Idolatry, or gross and indecent Corruptions; until people be first by the preaching of the true Doctrine per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swaded, willingly to part with them. But if this were to make Gods house a place of Merchandise for men, there to sell <ns0:hi>Oxen,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sheep,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Doves,</ns0:hi> and keep Shops for <ns0:hi>Changing money</ns0:hi>: What do Papists make such houses, by their shewing their <ns0:hi>Relicks</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Images</ns0:hi> to people, thereby to get money for their Priests; and for selling Pardons, Indulgences? <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Never were Gods Houses to that degree made places of Merchandises, and <ns0:hi>Dens of Thieves,</ns0:hi> if every one that cheateth for his profit be (as he is) a Theif.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And his disciples remembred that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Disciples, as well as the rest of the people there present, could not but be astonished at this so strange a thing, to see a single Person, and he in no repute but as a private Person, to make a Whip, and with authority drive the Buyers and Sellers out of the Temple, and no body to op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose him; but they remembred the words of <ns0:hi>David, Psal.</ns0:hi> 69.9. Some think that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> here reports what they did after Christs Resurrection; and indeed, who so considereth the following part of the <ns0:hi>Gospel History,</ns0:hi> would think that it were so; for they did not seem so early to have had a per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swasion of Christs Divine nature, nor that he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> Or if they at this time remembred it, and apprehended that Christ was the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> the Impression seems to have worn off. It is a greater Question, whether <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 69. (from whence this quotation is,) is to be understood of Christ, properly and literally? Or meerly as the <ns0:hi>Antitype</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> of whom that <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> is literally to be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood. Some of the <ns0:hi>Lutheranes</ns0:hi> think that <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> prima<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rily concerned Christ. Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin,</ns0:hi> and others, think it onely concerned Christ as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s antitype: The former for their Opinion, take notice of the frequent Quotation of it in the <ns0:hi>New Testament, Matth.</ns0:hi> 27.48. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 19.28. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.20. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.3. The other urge, that there are some things in that <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> which cannot agree to Christ. The matter is not much; <ns0:hi>Zeal</ns0:hi> is nothing but a warmth of <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Anger.</ns0:hi> It is good to be <ns0:hi>Zealous</ns0:hi>; yea, swal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed up with <ns0:hi>Zeal</ns0:hi> in a good cause; but men must take heed of the pharisaical Zeal, not according to <ns0:hi>Knowledg</ns0:hi>; Christ was zealous, but the cause was good.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:332" />18 ¶ Then answered the Jews <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> whether some of the <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> or the Priests, (who were more specially concerned for their profit) or the common people, or all together, is not said. They undertake not to justifie their fact, nor could they deny it, but they ask him what sign he could shew them, to justifie his Divine Authority. For this seemeth to have been their principle, That let Corruptions and Abuses in a Church be never so great, yet they were not to be reformed, but either by the ordinary Authority of the Magistrate, or by an extraordinary Authority from God. Such an extraordinary Authority they would acknowledg in <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> but they expected that those who pretented to such an extraordinary Divine Mission, should be able to confirm that <ns0:hi>Mission</ns0:hi> by some miraculous Operations, (as <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 4.30.) They had had no <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> now for 400 years amongst them; the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> required there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore a sign, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.22 The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> were at the same point with <ns0:hi>the</ns0:hi> first <ns0:hi>Reformers</ns0:hi>; but they mistook; for they brought no new Doctrine; but still cried, to the <ns0:hi>Law, and to the Testimony</ns0:hi>; and where the true Doctrine and Sacra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments are upheld, there is a <ns0:hi>true Church,</ns0:hi> which hath power to call and send out Preachers.</ns0:note>, and said unto him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 12.38. Chap. 6.30.</ns0:note>, What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things <ns0:hi>l</ns0:hi>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Jesus answered and said unto them <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 27.40. Mark 14.58. and 15.29.</ns0:note>, De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Our Saviour refuseth to give them any sign, but that of his Resurrection the third day from the Dead. This was the sign to which he afterwards referreth the Pharisees, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 12.39. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.29. Our Saviours words must not be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood, as commanding or licensing them to destroy him; but as foretelling what they would do. It is in Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, very ordinary to use the <ns0:hi>Imperative mood</ns0:hi> for the Future tense of the <ns0:hi>Indicative,</ns0:hi> see <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 42.18. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.50. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.9, 10. and 54. 1. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 13.27. <ns0:hi>Destroy,</ns0:hi> is as much as, I know you will destroy, or if you do destroy this Temple, I will build it up in three days. The Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection of Christ from the dead, is ordinarily in Scripture attributed to the Father; but here Christ saith he would do it, and the <ns0:hi>Spirit</ns0:hi> by whom he is said to have been quickned, equally proceedeth both from the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Son.</ns0:hi> Nor is this the onely Text, where it is attributed to Christ, see <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 20.17, 18. It was the work of the Tri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity, out of it self, and so the work of all the three Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons. These words were three years after this made a great charge against Christ, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.61. but they reported them thus: <ns0:hi>This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.</ns0:hi> He said onely, <ns0:hi>the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple,</ns0:hi> meaning his Body.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> understood his words of that material Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple in which they at this time were, which the best Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters think was the Temple builded by <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zero<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />babel</ns0:hi>: but how to make it out, that it was 46 years building, they were not well agreed.                      </ns0:gap> gave them a clearer insight into the Scriptures of the <ns0:hi>Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment,</ns0:hi> and the harmony of the writings of the <ns0:hi>Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment,</ns0:hi> with Christs words under the <ns0:hi>New Testament,</ns0:hi> confirm<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the Disciples Faith in both.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 ¶ Now when he was at Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast <ns0:hi>day,</ns0:hi> many believed in his Name <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">To believe in Christs name, and to believe in Christ himself, are one and the same thing; as it is the same to <ns0:hi>call upon God,</ns0:hi> and to call upon <ns0:hi>the Name of God</ns0:hi>: so <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 3.16. The meaning is, that they believed the things which were published concerning his Person and Office, yet the <ns0:hi>Periphrasis, Believing in his name,</ns0:hi> is not vain; but de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clareth a mutual relation betwixt God and the Word, by the Preaching of which he maketh himself known to the World. True faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God. I think it is to no purpose disputed here by some, Whether the Faith here mentioned was true Faith, yea or no. It appeareth by what followeth, that it was not true justifying Faith; but it was true in its kind. To make up true justifying saving Faith, which the Apostle calls <ns0:hi>the Faith of Gods elect,</ns0:hi> three things are required, 1. A knowledg of the Proposition of the Word revealing Christ; this is acquired by Reading, Hearing, Meditation, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> 2. The second i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Assent,</ns0:hi> which is the act of the understanding, agreeing in the truth of the word revealed, when such an Assent is given to a Proposition, if merely upon the Divine Revela<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of it; this is Faith, a true Faith in its kind. 3. Upon this now (in those who savingly believe), the Will closeth with Christ as an adequate object; for it receiveth him, accepteth him, relies on him as its Saviour, and moveth by the Affections, to Love, Desire, Hope, Rejoyce in him; and commandeth the outward man into an Obedience to his Law. Now it is very possible, that through a common Influence of the Holy Spirit of God, men upon the hearing of the Word; especially, having the advantage of seeing miraculous Operations confirming the Word, may give a true Assent to the Proposition of the Word, as a Propo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sition of Truth, and yet may never receive Christ as their Saviour, close with him, trust in him, desire, love, or o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bey him; this was the case of these Persons (many at least of them.)</ns0:note>, when they saw the miracles which he did <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">They <ns0:hi>believed, seeing the miracles which Christ did</ns0:hi>; they wanted a due knowledg of Christ founded in the Word; neither had they any certain, steady, fixed Assent, founded in the discerning the Truth of the Propo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sition; their Assent was sudden, founded onely upon the Miracles they saw wrought, so as tho they might have some confidence in him, as a famous Person, and some great Prince, from whom they might expect some earthly good; yet this was all, which was far enough from true saving Faith.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 But Jesus did not commit himself unto them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Christ did not take all these seeming Believers into his Bosom, nor call them after him, nor maintained any familiar fellowship and communion with them; but made hast again into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> till his time was come, knowing that in so pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lick a place of danger, they were not to be trusted;</ns0:note>, because he knew all men <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">for being God blessed for ever, he had knowledg of the hearts of all men,</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:332" />25 And needed not that any should testifie of man <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">And needed not any information concerning the Prin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples and Humours of all Men; for he perfectly knew men, not onely from their more external Acts and Behaviours, (as we know them); but he knew what was in them, search<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the hearts, and trying the reins, which is the property of God alone, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8.39. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 33.15. Here what we formerly observed, is again observable; that oft times in holy writ, for the further Confirmation of a Proposition, to an universal Affirmative is added, a contrary Negative. Here ariseth a question, agitated betwixt the <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Calvinists, Whether Christ as man knew all things, and what is in the heart of man</ns0:hi>; they affirm it, because of the <ns0:hi>personal Vnion of the Divine and Humane Nature in Christ.</ns0:hi> We say, that altho there be such a personal Union, yet the properties of each nature remain distinct; upon which account Christ denyeth that he, as the Son of Man, knew the day and hour of the end of the World. Besides, by the same reason, that <ns0:hi>Omniscience</ns0:hi> belongeth to the Humane Nature of Christ; <ns0:hi>Omnipotence, Infiniteness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Omnipresence</ns0:hi> also must; which last indeed they affirm, seeing that without it, they were not able to defend their Doctrine of <ns0:hi>Consubstantiation,</ns0:hi> or the presence of the Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy and Blood of Christ, wherever the Sacrament of his Supper is Administred; but this being a matter <ns0:hi>Polemi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cal,</ns0:hi> we shall not here discourse it.
